findings: F1-22-layer3: "An FPGA is slower and uses more power and area ... FPGAs are used for prototyping ... data centres" (D1, D3) → kept only "no manufacturing step: a new design is a new bitstream" (D6); the rest moved into the unverified box (D6 ch. 1)

F1-22-hardware: "In many FPGAs those cells are SRAM ... reloads its bitstream from a separate non-volatile memory chip at every power-up" → one vendor's family holds configuration in volatile memory and reloads after power-up, e.g. from external non-volatile memory; another family uses internal flash (D6 ch. 1; D9)
F1-22-layer2: "load it into the device, usually over USB from the development board" → load through a configuration interface such as JTAG; the board's documentation says how it connects (D6 ch. 1)
F1-22-answers: "a Verilog integer is a 32-bit variable" (D4) → the tools treat integer as 32 bits: Yosys made 32 flip-flops (standard text not opened) (R4)

F1-22-breaks: "Programmable wires are slower than fixed wires"; "Loading a bitstream stops the old circuit" → routes add delay that timing analysis checks; a new circuit is a new bitstream and stored values are not part of it (D11 §2; D6 ch. 1)

Not found: Programmable wires slower than fixed wires → reworded to timing analysis after place and route (D11).
